decisionsTitle: The highest and the lowest altitude on the bib's profile in the bib's band colour
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-11-17, looking at the race's bib** — a profile strip turned for the runner, with «Start», the kilometres «1», «2», «3», «km 4,5 · apă + hrană», «6», «7 km», «Sosire», and the altitudes «622 m» and «815 m»: «pe viitor: aș vrea ca numerele de la elevație să fie un pic colorate diferit, să nu se confunde cu markerii de distanță».

**What was there.** The strip's highest and lowest altitude — its `extremes` (§804): the highest above its point, the lowest in the foot row beside the kilometres or beside «Start» and «Sosire» — were set in the ink, the size and the weight of the kilometre labels, so «815 m» under the curve read like one more distance marker.

**Decision.** The two altitude labels are drawn in the bib's band colour: the colour that bib's own header band is drawn in, as the drawing already holds it — the event's `bib_colour`, the club's blue when the event names none, the members' colour on a member's bib with their band; under the club's header picture, the colour the band would have. Where that colour reads too light on the white paper — under 3 : 1 against white, computed as WCAG does (`BIB_LAYOUT.profileAltitudeContrast`) — they are drawn in the strip's ink at 60 % (`profileAltitudeOpacity`), which still reads at 4.5 : 1 on white and stands 3.8 : 1 apart from the kilometres' ink.

**A member's card.** A member's card («Tot numărul», §695) has no band: its strip stands, in white, on the card's own ground — the members' colour itself, the kit's gradient or their photograph under the veil — so its altitudes are always the card's white, faded, and held to the same bar as everywhere else: the white at 60 % where that reads at 3 : 1 on the card's ground, else stronger by 5 % at a time (`profileAltitudeOpacityStep`), up to the full white, at the first strength that does. Each renderer hands the function the card's background as it draws it (`bibMemberCardBackground`): the members' colour; the gradient, judged on both its stops; the photograph, judged by the veil over a white photograph, the lightest ground the veil can give. So 60 % on the gradient (6.5 : 1 and 4.0 : 1 on its two stops), on the veiled photograph (3.3 : 1 over a white one) and on the editor's purple (4.3 : 1) and black (6.6 : 1); 65 % on the red (3.1 : 1, where 60 % would read 2.9 : 1) and 70 % on the teal (3.0 : 1, where 60 % would read 2.6 : 1). The editor's green and orange never colour a card — white does not read on them at AA, and the card prints the gradient instead. Among the colours a card accepts (white on them at 4.5 : 1 or more, which an event's file may also bring), swept across the colour cube three levels at a time, none needed more than 80 %. The price is the gap to the kilometres, which are the full white: 1.5 : 1 on the teal, 1.8 : 1 on the red and over a white photograph, 2 : 1 or more on the other grounds — less than the paper's 3.8 : 1, still a step the eye sees, and never bought by reading less than 3 : 1.

**The club's colour gives the band's colour.** The club's blue reads at 9.9 : 1 on white, and each of the six colours the editor offers reads at 3 : 1 or more (the orange the least, 3.1 : 1), so every band the editor offers gives the band's colour; only a lighter colour an event can still carry — from an event's file, a yellow say — gives the ink at 60 %. The black the editor offers passes too and prints the altitudes in a black close to the ink (1.07 : 1 between them): the rule as decided, said here so a black race is not a surprise.

**One function, both renderers.** `bib-profile-strip.ts#bibAltitudeInk({ band, ink, card })` decides it — `card` is a member's card's background, or nothing for a bib on the white paper — and both drawings ask it with what they already hold for the bib: the sheet (`bibs-pdf.ts`, the two altitudes filled last, as ever, inside a saved state so nothing after them is faint) and the picture (`bib-image.tsx`, the two words' boxes carry the colour, and an opacity only below 1), so they cannot disagree. The strip marks its two altitude words (`BibStripText.altitude`). Nothing else changes: their size, weight and place; the kilometre labels and their unit; «Start» and «Sosire»; the checkpoints' words and glyphs; the curve, its area and the scale's ticks; the phones' line. `BIB_DRAWING_VERSION` is 10, so every stamped preview — the bibs page's and the desk's — is drawn again.

**Why only the altitudes.** They are the one pair of numbers on the strip that is not a distance. Colouring the kilometres instead would change every mark a runner reads to find the next aid station, and colouring both would separate nothing.

**Not done.** The event page's elevation chart and the editor's chart keep their colours — the owner spoke of the bib; the kilometres' colour; a colour of their own for the altitudes on a member's card — on a ground of any colour the card's white, faded, is the one ink that reads; a design option to choose the altitudes' colour (the band's colour, or the ink faded, is the rule, not a choice); any other text on the bib.

**Held by** `tests/unit/registrations/bib-altitude-colour.test.ts` — the rule either side of 3 : 1, the club's blue and the editor's six colours; a member's card on the kit's gradient and on the veiled photograph, on every colour the editor offers that a card carries, and on every colour a card accepts in a sweep of the colour cube, each at the faintest strength that reads; the sheet read through pdfkit's `fillColor`, `fillOpacity`, `save` and `restore`: the two altitudes and nothing else the sheet writes in the band's colour, the profile turned or not, under the club's header picture too, the ink at 60 % for them alone under a yellow band, the members' colour on a member's bib, and on a member's card its white at the strength its ground needs — 60 % on the purple, the black, the gradient, the green that prints the gradient and a white photograph under the veil, 65 % on the red, 70 % on the teal; the picture's markup carrying the same ink, the red card's 65 % included; the sheet and the picture asking the function the same question for an ordinary bib, a member's band, a member's card in the purple, in the red and on the gradient, and an elite bib; and the picture's pixels — the band's colour on the altitudes and nowhere else under the header, and under a yellow band each pixel of the altitudes 60 % as dark as the same pixel drawn in the full ink — and by the drawing's fingerprint in `bib-figures-place.test.ts`, captured again: with the altitudes' colour forced back to the ink (the function made to answer the ink, and the picture's strip handed the ink) the call gives §959's hash again, «48afc92f…dfef79d», so the colour is the one change.
changelogLine: - **The bib's altitudes in the bib's own colour** — on the route's profile the highest and the lowest altitude («815 m», «622 m») now print in the colour of the bib's band — the club's blue unless the race chose another, the members' colour on a member's bib — so they no longer read like one more kilometre; a colour too light for small type on white prints them in the ink at 60 % instead. Nothing else on the strip changes. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given a bib design that draws the route's profile from the GPX with «Kilometrii și altitudinile pe profil», when a number is printed or previewed, then the strip's highest and lowest altitude are drawn in the colour of that bib's own header band — the event's, the club's when the event names none, the members' on a member's bib with their band — or, where that colour reads under 3 : 1 against white as WCAG computes it, in the strip's ink at 60 %; on a member's card, in the card's white at 60 %, or at the first strength above it, 5 % at a time, that reads at 3 : 1 on the card's own ground (its colour, both stops of its gradient, the veil over a white photograph); on the sheet and in the picture alike, from one function; every other word of the strip, its curve, its pins and its scale keep the ink, the altitudes keep their size, weight and place, and the pictures' addresses change with the drawing's version (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the bib's altitudes in the band's colour
